_comment: Rules of skill F. A rule computes only if VERIFIED-REOPENED. Engineering rules (independence of a reproduction, link grading, class coverage) carry no external claim and are described in scripts/mechanism_check.py.

rules.passage: ARRIVE 2.0 (Percie du Sert et al., PLOS Biology 2020), opened in full 7 Nov 2026: the "ARRIVE Essential 10" "constitutes the minimum requirement" and the "Recommended Set" "describes the research context". Items in the page: Study design; Sample size; Inclusion and exclusion criteria; Randomisation; Blinding; Outcome measures; Statistical methods; Experimental animals; Experimental procedures; Results.

FDA-NIH BEST glossary, opened in full 7 Nov 2026: "Pharmacodynamic biomarker: A response biomarker that indicates biologic activity of a medical product or environmental agent without necessarily drawing conclusions about efficacy or disease outcome or necessarily linking this activity to an established mechanism of action."

Minikel et al., Nature 2024, opened in full 7 Nov 2026: "We estimate the probability of success for drug mechanisms with genetic support is 2.6 times greater than those without." Context only; never applied to an asset; authors include employees of the funder of the work (Deerfield, Genscience).

Seok et al., PNAS 2013: murine orthologs "are close to random in matching their human counterparts (e.g., R2 between 0.0 and 0.1)" for acute inflammatory stresses. A dispute of the conclusion is possible but was not located (F12); the figure is not applied to any model.

National Academies (2019), Executive Summary: replicability is "obtaining consistent results across studies aimed at answering the same scientific question, each of which has obtained its own data"; the assessment of replicability "may not result in a binary pass/fail answer; rather ... the degree to which one result replicates another". The source does not define independence by organization; that part of the plugin rule is an ENGINEERING RULE.

ARRIVE 2.0 Explanation and Elaboration: measurements from 50 cells of one mouse represent n = 1 when the experimental unit is the mouse; reporting n = 50 "is an example of pseudoreplication" that "underestimates the true variability" and "can lead to false positives"; the report should state n per group and per experiment, including any independent replications.

Radic et al. 2026 (narrative review): regulatory class-wide warnings rest on shared target biology; extrapolation "does not prove identical toxicity across compounds"; the arguments for a class effect "support class-wide vigilance, not proof of uniform class toxicity". The strongest causal evidence remains specific to one molecule; signals for others derive mainly from pharmacovigilance and less comparable datasets.

FDA draft guidance (September 2025, Revision 1; DRAFT, not final): the guidance describes how FDA reviews and acts on safety labeling changes when new safety information applies to multiple application holders and the change is issued to multiple applicants; FDA may receive multiple supplements and harmonize the language. The word 'class' is not used. Context only.
